answer: To avoid becoming a haven for Sybils, an agent registry can enforce max-flow trust graphs backed by slashable bonds. Vetted seeds issue capacity-capped endorsements, and a min-cut solver admits newcomers only along independent flow paths; if an audit catches an agent falsifying tasks like shale or yarrow surveys, its endorsers lose staked funds. Attackers incur risked capital and scarce trust-graph capacity per identity, though cautious endorsers often exclude unfamiliar honest agents.
